name: 21809-longcontext-8b-1gpu
hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 on an a3 node (--gres=gpu:1), sm90, driver 570.195.03.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. ONE in-process vLLM engine, one GPU.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=2, no warmup and no cooldown, bounded at 2 requests with a 5400 s safety cap -- the source's own `--num-prompts 2 --max-concurrency 2`.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets. Prompt exactly 120000 tokens and output exactly 1000 (min = max on both), no shared prefix, seed 21809. Sampling is temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0, ignore_eos true, so every request generates all 1000 tokens. `request_format: plain` means no chat template.
purpose: An 8B-parameter research assistant digesting 120,000-token documents into 1,000-token briefs, two concurrent requests on one GPU.
launch:
# One GPU serving a small dense model very long prompts with moderate generations: 120000 tokens
# in, 1000 out, two offered at once. Nothing here is tuned.

# meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is GATED; this is NousResearch's ungated mirror of the same
# release, config.json identical field for field.
model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct

tensor-parallel-size: 1

# The checkpoint's own native window, pinned rather than lowered because it also acts as a floor
# guard: the engine refuses to start unless one max-length sequence fits the KV pool (131072
# tokens = 16.0 GiB), so a memory budget that came out too small fails loudly at startup.
max-model-len: 131072

enable-chunked-prefill: true
enable-prefix-caching: false

# BOTH MUST BE PINNED HERE OR THE ENGINE WILL NOT BUILD: at this commit each is declared
# `SkipValidation[int] = None` with no static default, and the table that fills them in is keyed
# on a usage context the in-process engine path does not supply, so `_verify_args` raises.
# 8192 is what `vllm serve` itself resolves to on this card at this commit; 128 is an ordinary
# serving value and is not binding at 2 streams.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
max-num-seqs: 128

# The checkpoint's own torch_dtype, named so a default cannot drift the weight width.
dtype: bfloat16

# 0.55 RATHER THAN THE USUAL 0.90, and it is the one value in this file that is not ordinary.
# At 128 KiB of KV per token, 0.90 on an 80 GB H100 gives roughly 53 GiB of pool (~434,000
# tokens); 0.55 gives 43.8 GiB of budget, less ~15.0 GiB of weights and roughly 4-6 GiB of
# non-torch memory, activation peak and captured graphs, leaving order 22-27 GiB of KV -- about
# 180,000 to 220,000 tokens. Do not raise it without re-reading max-model-len above, which sets
# the floor at 131,072 tokens.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.55
